title: Campus Bikes
summary: Given a campus represented on the X-Y plane with n workers and m bikes (n <= m), assign a bike to each worker by choosing the pair with the shortest Manhattan distance.
statement: Given a campus represented on the X-Y plane with n workers and m bikes (n <= m), assign a bike to each worker by choosing the pair with the shortest Manhattan distance. If distances are equal, prioritize the worker with the smallest index, and if still equal, the bike with the smallest index. Continue until all workers are assigned a bike. Return an array indicating the assigned bike index for each worker.
constraints: Assign one distinct bike per worker.
Process pairs by distance, then worker index, then bike index.
hints: The problem defines one global ordering over every worker-bike pair.
Accept a tuple only when both its worker and bike remain unassigned.
Scanning the exact priority order makes each accepted assignment the mandated next choice.
editorial: Scanning the exact priority order makes each accepted assignment the mandated next choice.

tests.explanation: The globally ordered pairs assign bike one to worker zero and bike zero to worker one.
Tie-breaking by worker and bike indices determines the assignment.
